Posted by Hasan Shodiev 
 
Edited 
Tutorial Component 
The tutorial component is held every week and is designed to support students in 
developing strong conceptual understanding, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills 
in physics. 
Tutorials provide a structured and supportive environment in which students actively 
engage with physics problems related to the course material. Each session focuses on 
reasoning, application, and analysis, rather than passive review. 
During tutorials, we work through carefully selected problems together. Students receive 
real-time guidance and feedback, encouraging them to: 
• Think critically about physical situations in a variety of contexts 
• Apply physics concepts with increasing confidence 
• Refine the accuracy, clarity, and coherence of the reasoning 
This iterative, hands-on problem-solving process strengthens conceptual foundations and 
cultivates a methodical scientific mindset—skills essential for success in both academic 
studies and professional scientific or technical fields.

Tutorial Section Month Day Time 
PC141 -T02 January 9 Friday 10:30 am – 11:20 am 
(Please attend only the tutorial section for which you are registered.) 
 
Preparation and Materials 
To ensure productive and focused tutorial sessions, students are expected to come 
prepared. Please bring the following to every tutorial, starting with the first one: 
• Your physics textbook and/or lecture notes 
• A scientific calculator 
• A notebook for handwritten problem solving and short quizzes 
 
Digital Tools Policy 
In alignment with the laboratory philosophy and to promote independent reasoning and 
authentic learning, digital devices are not permitted during tutorial sessions. 
This includes cell phones, laptops, tablets, and smart devices, which must be turned off for 
the entire tutorial. 
Tutorials are intentionally designed as spaces for focused thinking, manual problem 
solving, and direct engagement with physics concepts, particularly important in the era of 
powerful digital and AI-based tools. 
 
Communication 
Please do not send messages through MyLearningSpace. 
 You can reach me at hshodiev@wlu.ca using your myLaurier webmail account only. 
When emailing, include your course code and tutorial section in the subject line 
(e.g., PC141 – Tutorial Section T02). 
Emails without proper course and section identification may not receive a response.

I look forward to meeting you in the tutorials and working with you throughout the term. 
• Tutorial Policies and Procedures 
Posted by Hasan Shodiev 
 
Edited 
The policies governing the tutorial portion of this course are the same as those for the 
laboratory portion, unless otherwise stated below. This alignment ensures consistency in 
expectations, academic integrity, and professional conduct across all instructional 
formats. 
Where necessary, additional policies specific to the tutorial format are outlined in this 
section. 
Office Hours 
Office Hours: 
Room R2089 
Thursdays, 4:00 pm – 6:00 pm 
Tutorial Format 
Tutorials are held every week and are designed as active problem-solving sessions. 
The general tutorial format is as follows: 
Open-Book Written Tutorial Report 
• Tutorials typically involve the completion of a written, in-class tutorial report 
• The report must reflect your own independent reasoning and work 
Permitted Resources 
Only the following resources are allowed during the tutorial: 
• Scientific calculator 
• Course textbook, if printed 
• Lecture notes

text:
• Homework and tutorial notes 
Use of any other resources (including unauthorized digital tools, online resources, or AI-
based systems) will result in a grade of zero for that week’s tutorial report, and may lead to 
more severe academic penalties. 
 
Instructional Support During Tutorials 
• Instructional Assistants (IAs) are available during tutorials to answer general 
questions and provide guidance. 
• IAs will not provide complete solutions, but will help clarify concepts, 
methods, and common pitfalls. 
• Occasionally, tutorials may explore applications or examples beyond those 
covered in lecture, to deepen understanding and broaden perspective. 
 
Preparation Expectations 
To be successful in tutorials, students are expected to follow this preparation sequence 
each week: 
10. Attend all lectures 
11. Review lecture material and attempt assigned problems 
12. Seek help early if needed: 
o Attend office hours 
o Consult your classmates 
13. Carefully review feedback from previous tutorials and labs 
Take note of mistakes and ensure they are not repeated 
Consistent preparation is essential for meaningful participation and steady progress. 
 
Attendance and Grading Policies 
14. Attendance at the tutorial section in which you are registered is compulsory.

text:
15. If you must miss a tutorial, email me once before the session when possible; all 
follow-up will be handled in person during your next lab/tut. Illness-based make-ups 
require a doctor’s or walk-in clinic note; varsity travel needs an official athletics 
confirmation; other reasons require appropriate documentation. Make-ups are arranged 
within one week given section capacity and safety constraints. 
Please do not send sensitive medical details—bring documentation to the lab/tut. 
16. Tutorial grades will be posted on MyLearningSpace (MyLS). 
17. The final tutorial grade will be determined out of 100%, based on the weighting 
specified in the course outline. 
18. Any concerns regarding marking or grade recording must be raised within one week 
of the work being marked. 
o Contact your section IA first before contacting me. 
o No grade changes will be made after this period 
 
Academic Integrity in Tutorials 
Students are encouraged to actively engage in discussion and problem-solving during 
tutorial sessions. Collaboration in understanding concepts is welcomed. 
However: 
• All submitted tutorial reports must represent your own independent work 
• Copying, reproducing, or transcribing another student’s work—either in 
whole or in part—constitutes academic dishonesty 
• Any form of cheating will be handled in accordance with the University’s 
Academic Integrity Policy and may result in disciplinary action 
Maintaining academic honesty is essential to the learning process and to the integrity of 
the course.
